question.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}{e}^{xyz}+{y}^{2},$ find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0).$
question.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(1,-2,0).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{xyz}+{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{xyz}+{y}^{2})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}{e}^{xyz}+{y}^{2})\,k \\  & =(2x+{x}^{2}yz){e}^{xyz}\,i+({x}^{3}z{e}^{xyz}+2y)\,j+{x}^{3}y{e}^{xyz}\,k \\ ∇f(1,-2,0) & =(2(1)+({1}^{2})(-2)(0)){e}^{1(-2)(0)}\,i+(({1}^{3})(0){e}^{1(-2)(0)}+2(-2))\,j+({1}^{3})(-2){e}^{1(-2)(0)}\,k \\  & =2\,i-4\,j-2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $2\,i-4\,j-2\,k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-2,0).$
